title: AI Engineer (GenAI end to end)
blurb: Build and ship LLM products end to end: programming and ML foundations, how models work, prompting and APIs, embeddings and RAG, agents and MCP, AI UX, evals and LLMOps, safety, fine-tuning, serving and cost, and GenAI system design.
audience: Software engineers moving into AI engineering or GenAI product roles

nodes.title: Python for AI work
nodes.summary: Comfortable Python: typing, async, virtual environments, notebooks and calling HTTP APIs. Almost every AI library and interview take-home is Python-first.
checklist: Set up a project with a virtual environment and pinned dependencies (uv or venv plus pip)
Use type hints, dataclasses and Pydantic models for request and response data
Write list and dict comprehensions, generators and context managers fluently
Read and write JSON, JSONL and CSV files without loading huge files into memory
Call a REST API with httpx or requests, handling timeouts and non-2xx responses
Structure a small package with modules, a CLI entry point and pytest tests

links.title: uv: Python package and project manager

nodes.title: TypeScript for AI apps
nodes.summary: Most AI product surfaces are web apps, so TypeScript with runtime validation is the second language of AI engineering. Types catch wiring bugs; schemas catch bad model output.

Explain why a TypeScript type alone does not protect you at runtime

nodes.title: Async I/O, concurrency and HTTP APIs

checklist: Run many LLM calls concurrently with asyncio.gather or Promise.all and cap concurrency with a semaphore or pool

Retry 429 and 5xx responses with exponential backoff and jitter, but never retry 400s
Consume a server-sent events stream and explain why SSE suits token streaming
Explain idempotency keys and why retries can double-charge or double-act
Expose an async endpoint (FastAPI or a Next.js route handler) that streams a response
